question.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mrow> <mn>150</mn><mi> g</mi></mrow> </math> of water at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is contained in a thermally insulated container. Now the air from the vessel is pumped out adiabatically. A fraction of water gets converted into ice and the remaining evaporates at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0 </mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> itself. The mass of evaporated water will be closest to [Take the latent heat of vaporization of water, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>L</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mo>kg</mo><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and latent heat of fusion of water, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>L</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>kg</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>]

solution.text:
Let us assume the mass of the water evaporated is m, then

mLv=150-mLf

m×2.1×106=150-m×3.36×105

On solving we get

m≈20 g
